newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT APPROVES EXCISE TAX HIKES.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT APPROVES EXCISE TAX HIKES.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Thursday that it has decided to increase excise taxes on fuel, tobacco and alcohol products from April 15.
The duty on petroleum will be raised to 800 litas per tonne from 560 litas, Vaclovas Medishauskas, the government's advisor on financial issues, told Reuters.
He added that the excise taxes for jet fuel, kerosene and heating fuel will increase to 300 litas per tonne from 190 litas.
He said that the government also decided at its weekly cabinet session on Wednesday to introduce a uniform excise duty of 12 litas per 1,000 cigarettes on all brands.
The tax currently ranges from five to 15 litas depending on the quality of the brand.
The 15 litas excise duty on high-quality brands will remain in effect until September 30, Medishauskas said.
The duty on spirits will be raised from 0.30 litas per percentage of alcohol to 0.43 litas.
The duty on mead will be raised to 0.12 litas for every percent of alcohol in the product from 0.10 litas.
The duty on wine products with an alcohol content of between 13 and 18 percent will be increased to 0.17 litas from 0.15 litas.
The excise tax on champagne and sparkling wine will jump to 0.35 litas from 0.25 litas.
